title: Migrate Add-on Services catalogue to operation-backend

input.requestedOutcome: Wire the durable Add-on Services catalogue to operation-backend in operations mode without mapping custom booking add-on types.
acceptanceCriteria: GET /v1/addon-services?active=all replaces the operations-mode service projection.
Create, edit, complete variant replacement, and delete use the documented API routes.
Successful responses update memory/UI only after the server accepts the mutation; failed writes leave the projection unchanged and surface an error.
Legacy mode remains delegated to the original functions and classic script order is preserved.
SB_ADDON_TYPES and booking-priced add-on data are not mapped or mutated.
constraints: No backend, schema, migration, mapping, database, or DDL changes.
Use laOps/laOpsFetch through the existing core client; no direct fetch.
Preserve server-first operations behavior and legacy fallback.
Do not modify shared legacy renderer files or excluded parity files.
assumptions: 00-ops-core.js provides serialized writes and visible error reporting.
The legacy Add-on Services functions are defined before the ops adapter tag.
Backend contracts are the handlers/domain in operation-backend sales-editing.ts and addon-services.ts.

output.summary: Added an operations-only Add-on Services adapter with authoritative server loading, server-first service and variant mutations, legacy fallback, and an explicit exclusion of custom booking add-on types.

filesChanged.purpose: Map the legacy Add-on Services renderer and handlers to /v1/addon-services in operations mode.
Load the S4 adapter after the existing rate-type adapter and before ops boot.
Verify API mapping, list/create/variant-replace/delete, failed-write rollback, exclusion, and legacy fallback.
Durable S4 implementation, contract, verification, and rollback report.

behaviorChanges.before: The configuration screen used a RAM-only local seed.
behaviorChanges.after: Operations mode loads active and inactive services from the server and replaces the legacy projection.

behaviorChanges.before: Legacy handlers mutated RAM without a durable operation-backend path.
behaviorChanges.after: Create, service edit, variant full-list replacement, and delete call documented API routes and reconcile only after success.

behaviorChanges.before: The operations migration had no S4 service adapter.
behaviorChanges.after: Legacy mode is unchanged, and SB_ADDON_TYPES/custom booking add-on types are untouched.

changed: operations-mode renderAddonSvc and aos* service/variant handlers
legacy service shape ↔ Add-on Service API mapping

details: Operations-mode SB_ADDON_SVCS is replaced from API responses and is not written to localStorage.
Failed operations leave the in-memory server projection unchanged.
Custom booking add-on type state is neither read nor mutated by this adapter.

verification.evidence: 4 passed, 0 failed; list/create/variant replacement/delete, failed-write rollback, custom-type exclusion, and legacy delegation covered.
581 total: 573 passed, 0 failed, 8 skipped; includes sales-editing Add-on Services route coverage.

decisions: Load active=all because the configuration screen must display inactive services too.
Send the complete variants array on variant changes because the backend PATCH contract replaces the list as one fact.
Keep custom booking add-on types on the legacy path; this adapter contains no SB_ADDON_TYPES mapping or persistence.
Use the server response as the only successful service projection update; DELETE 204 removes the local row only after acceptance.
risks: Variant replacement has no verified frontend concurrency token and may race another editor; a later server reload remains authoritative.
Legacy agent-level addonServices cleanup was not copied because no server association contract was verified and the packet excludes booking-priced add-on mapping.
followUps: Audit a separate backend contract before migrating custom booking add-on types.
rollback: Revert the S4 local commit or remove the S4 script tag, adapter, focused test, and handoff artifacts; do not issue compensating destructive API calls.
